newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM, Chechen leader agree joint statement.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM, Chechen leader agree joint statement.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev signed a joint declaration of principles on Thursday aimed at ending the conflict in Chechnya, Russian news agencies said.

Quoting sources close to the prime minister, Interfax reported Chernomyrdin as saying the document was "a big step in the right direction". Itar-Tass said a joint commission would be charged with a range of tasks including rebuilding the Chechen economy.
The agencies said Russian security chief Alexander Lebed also signed the document. He signed an original peace accord on August 31 with Chechen chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov.
Chernomyrdin, Yandarbiyev, Lebed and other officials met for an hour and a half in Moscow.
Interfax later quoted the prime minister as saying the joint commission would comprise "people of authority, capable of settling issues by themselves".

The commission's main tasks, he said, would be the rebuilding of the economy, cooperating in the process of setting up new government structures in the region and organising elections to a local parliament.
